answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing when they have more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player. Tokens and the Vagabond pawn do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie win ties if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop another player ruling.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Rule (2.5).

answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Rule (2.5).

answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from a clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing; you must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move (4.2).

answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move (4.2).

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; rule is not required. Defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise defender deals two immediate hits, uncapped by warriors, then discards it. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them), roll (higher die attacker, lower defender; ties equal; each side's rolled hits capped by its own warriors), after-roll effects (attacker orders if both), count hits (add extra hits, subtract ignored hits; if defender has no warriors attacker gets one defenseless hit; Vagabond instead is defenseless with no undamaged swords), then deal hits. The hit-taking side chooses removal order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens, and orders its own removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were removed after the roll. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores 1 VP each, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.

answer.part: Crafting costs, reuse, absent item supply, duplicates
answer.ruling: Crafting pieces take their suit from the clearing they occupy, and each required icon is paid by a matching workshop (Marquise), roost (Eyrie), or sympathy (Alliance); each piece activates only once per turn. Vagabond pays each icon by flipping one face-up, undamaged hammer face down; its clearing must match every icon, and it may reuse its pawn but must pay a hammer per icon each time. A three-color question-mark accepts any suit. An item card cannot be crafted if its matching item token is absent from map supply. Only an identical persistent effect already in your own play area blocks crafting it again; another player's copy does not.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1).

answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1).

answer.ruling: During your own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, matching mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.

When a dominance card would enter discard, put it near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it requires a bird card; a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking and activating are separate and neither uses a faction action allowance.

With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal three cards to each player. Cover four R slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, hide one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer, sword, one beneath each ruin, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return them to empty R slots; without Vagabond, ruins have no items. Set factions up in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond letter order; that is distinct from turn order.
answer.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup, hidden ruin items.

answers.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup, hidden ruin items.

answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply, including removals outside battle. Without a Keep, there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order except Recruit's once-per-turn limit. March is a compound action of up to two moves; do not interrupt it to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open slot and building type; take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the column cost by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP exposed on its track. Building requires full wood cost, a building available, and a legal slot.

In order: Emergency Orders (if hand empty, draw one); Add to Decree (must add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns); A New Roost. If no roost is on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column: Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose card order within a column freely. For each card: Recruit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at one chosen roost there (Charismatic must place two); Move matches origin and moves at least one warrior by ordinary path/rule requirements; Battle matches battle clearing and initiates battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build matches target and places a roost in a clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. Birds are wild in every column. If a required action cannot be completed, immediately Turmoil; cannot skip or continue.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight, resolve the Decree.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight, resolve the Decree.

answer.ruling: Lose 1 VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard all Decree cards except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none face up, turn all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends, but full normal Evening follows: score roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Turmoil; Evening, even after turmoil.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Turmoil; Evening, even after turmoil.

answer.ruling: Each time another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If no matching card including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming card, but payment or the no-match draw still occurs. Merely battling there does not trigger it unless sympathy is removed.

Both happen in Birdsong; complete all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy, and once spreading begins no return to Revolt that Birdsong. For either, every supporter spent must match target clearing; birds are wild. Revolt: choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces, score 1 VP per enemy building/token, place matching base, then place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy clearings (including this one) and one warrior in Officers. Spread: choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; spend supporters shown above next sympathy token plus one matching supporter if a single other player has at least three warriors there (Martial Law); place sympathy and score uncovered VP. Each clearing can have only one sympathy; Keep placement ban applies.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong: Revolt; Spread Sympathy.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong: Revolt; Spread Sympathy.

answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Each officer allows one Evening military operation, and operations do not consume officers. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score uncovered VP; no supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost, but token placement must be legal. Losing a base discards all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, removes half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discards excess supporters down to five.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Losing a base; Daylight; Evening.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Losing a base; Daylight; Evening.

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, Move and Rest
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh flips two exhausted items face up per tea already face up on Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed now gives no bonus. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in forest, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel face up; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items, and ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coins on track, even after Rest.

Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel/track, scores 1 VP if an item is taken, and removes the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot. Quest: in matching clearing choose face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, put it in completed quests, then choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special Allied-warrior battle-loss comparison. On Vagabond's own turn, battle Infamy adds 1 VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status; hostile building/token therefore gives 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy, while ordinary warrior removal scores no VP. No Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though it can still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors there may another faction piece be removed; it is not battle and scores no Infamy.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Relationships / Hostile; Daylight Aid and Strike; Scoring ordinary removal VP.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Relationships / Hostile; Daylight Aid and Strike; Scoring ordinary removal VP.

answer.ruling: With four or more players, Vagabond may during own Daylight at 10+ VP activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition, whose VP is lowest among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Place score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring; if partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.

Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play; faction rules prevail over incompatible general rules. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so a card can override it only if it explicitly does so; an ordinary card without an explicit override cannot.

answer.part: Unclear simultaneous choices and March interruption
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses; for battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

At-start effects precede all other effects of that phase; at-end effects follow everything else in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public but contents private; reveal/show only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards / hand information.

answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards / hand information.

answer.ruling: When shared deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. If instructed to give/discard a non-bird suit, birds must be treated as that suit. Only a bird card pays an explicit bird-card requirement; fox/rabbit/mouse cannot.

answer.part: Placement shortage, proxies, costs and Decree
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite; no proxies. If instructed to place more pieces than available, place the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily place fewer. A shortage never waives costs/prerequisites or Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions; if an Eyrie required action cannot be fully completed, it Turmoils.

Pieces normally are placed from supply or leftmost track space and removed to supply or rightmost empty track space. Removed items leave the game permanently. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Actions — shared rules; Special Rules — Place/remove/replace.

answers.evidence: Actions — shared rules; Special Rules — Place/remove/replace.

answer.ruling: Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: Replace in Keep and swap distinction
answer.ruling: An enemy cannot replace a piece in the Keep clearing if that would violate the rule that only Marquise may place pieces there; replacement requires both removal and placement to be possible. A swap ignores move/place restrictions, unlike a move or place.
If multiple players reach 30 simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river divides forests as paths do. Fall has no special rules.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Overview / setup.

answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Overview / setup.

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put Keep in any corner; put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop, recruiter among Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

Supply 10 warriors; place three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional face-down cards into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Vagabond starting setup besides hidden ruin items
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger; place pawn in any forest; shuffle quests and display three face up. Take character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Set each other faction's relationship marker to Indifferent.
Suggested minimum reach is 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law allows any mix totaling at least 17 for adventurous groups.

In Birdsong place one wood per sawmill (one per sawmill if multiple in a clearing); Daylight Overwork spends a card matching the sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both draw from finite supply of eight wood. Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Wood production; Evening.

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Wood production; Evening.

answer.ruling: Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, once per turn. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available and Marquise chooses among eligible recruiters where to place them.
Eyrie-crafted items score 1 VP rather than printed VP due to Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Lords of the Forest / Disdain for Trade; leader table.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Lords of the Forest / Disdain for Trade; leader table.

answer.ruling: Builder: Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP in addition to ordinary removal points.

No. Charismatic Recruit must place two warriors at one chosen roost. If the required action cannot be fully completed for any reason, including warrior supply, immediately Turmoil; cannot place only one as fulfillment.
Guerrilla War does not bypass warrior limits. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower; rolled hits remain capped by each side's warriors in battle.

Alliance can inspect Supporters; they are separate face-down stack, spent only for suit. They are not hand cards and do not count toward hand limit. Crafting is from hand, and Supporters are not stated as crafting cards.
No. All Revolts must be completed before Spread Sympathy begins. After spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Martial Law across multiple factions and Organize
answer.ruling: No: Martial Law applies if one other player has at least three warriors in the chosen clearing; two warriors from each of two players do not meet it. Martial Law adds one matching supporter to Spread Sympathy cost. Organize has no Martial Law cost.

Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it. But moving warriors into a sympathetic clearing does; allied warriors accompanying Vagabond movement into sympathy trigger Outrage, with the moving player paying one matching hand card per affected move.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Outrage; Vagabond Allied benefits.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Outrage; Vagabond Allied benefits.

answer.ruling: Available operations are Move, Battle, Recruit, Organize. Take up to your number of officers in operations, in any order and repetition; operations do not consume officers. Recruit places one warrior at one clearing with a base. After operations, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discard to five.
The pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead damage three Vagabond items.

answer.part: Vagabond hit limits and excess hits
answer.ruling: Maximum rolled hits equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Daylight Battle.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Daylight Battle.

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately go to empty matching tracks if possible; each track holds at most three. Exhausting a track item sends it to Satchel. Damaging an item moves it to Damaged without changing its face. Damaged items cannot pay actions even if face up.

Satchel plus Damaged box may hold six items plus two per face-up bag on its track; track items do not count. Check capacity last in Evening, after draw and discard; permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. No immediate check on acquiring items.

answer.part: Forest Rest versus Refresh and Repair
answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. It does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Birdsong Refresh flips exhausted items according to tea plus three; Repair exhausts hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening.

answer.part: Aid cost, target and relationship advance
answer.ruling: Aid exhausts one face-up undamaged item of any type and gives a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there, including Hostile. Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items into Satchel/track if available; no crafted item is required just to Aid. For a non-Hostile faction, advance one relationship space by Aiding that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; one Aid counts toward only one improvement.

At Allied status, each subsequent Aid scores 2 VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany its movement to destination, following their own movement restrictions; moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At start of battle as attacker, may treat warriors of one Allied faction in battle clearing as own, adding them to undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits. They may attack a different enemy; cannot use them to attack their own faction.

answer.part: Hostility from taking hits with allied warriors
answer.ruling: In a battle using allied warriors as your own, if Vagabond removes more allied warriors than items it damages in that battle, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it. This special timing overrides ordinary hostility timing for those allied warriors taken as hits against another enemy.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Taking hits with an ally.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Taking hits with an ally.

answer.part: Vagabond mixed-suit crafting and immediate use
answer.ruling: No, a single current clearing must match all crafting icons, so one clearing cannot pay mixed fox and rabbit. Exhaust one face-up undamaged hammer per icon; pawn may be reused repeatedly for multiple crafts despite normal once-per-turn limit, paying for every icon each time. When Vagabond crafts an item, it may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action if cost and requirements are met.

Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in your clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching clearing (bird qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces, then immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

When Explore takes the last hidden item, remove the ruin and free its building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed, so ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin; the Build procedure requires an open slot.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Vagabond — Explore.

answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Vagabond — Explore.

answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers; therefore a partner cannot be attacked as an enemy under ordinary battle requirements. If partner is Hostile, coalition resets marker to Indifferent.

Two warriors: 0 ordinary removal VP; the first warrior removed from a previously non-Hostile faction makes it Hostile and is excluded from Infamy. The second warrior is Hostile when removed and earns 1 Infamy VP. Building: 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP as a Hostile piece removed in battle on Vagabond's turn. Total = 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 VP.
answer.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — ordinary removal VP; Vagabond — Hostile / Infamy.

answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — ordinary removal VP; Vagabond — Hostile / Infamy.

answer.ruling: Into hostile buildings only: one boot, because hostility adds a boot only for hostile warriors. Into hostile warriors from several factions: two boots total—one normal plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction, not one extra per faction.
Taking an available dominance card only puts it in hand; it does not activate it. Taking and activating are separate Daylight procedures, and neither uses a Marquise action allowance.

Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns chosen faction and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

Resolve an immediate-effect card, then discard that crafting card to shared discard; a persistent-effect card stays in your play area. A card in play area is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play matching Ambush for two immediate hits; attacker may play matching Ambush to foil defending ambush. Dominance may be activated to change victory condition or spent for suit.
answer.evidence: Actions — Craft; Ambush cards cannot be crafted; Dominance cards cannot be crafted.

answers.evidence: Actions — Craft; Ambush cards cannot be crafted; Dominance cards cannot be crafted.

answer.part: Starting player, seating, markers, dice, setup order
answer.ruling: Randomly determine starting player and seating; take faction boards/pieces and select Fall or Winter. Place score markers at 0; battle dice are placed nearby. Faction setup proceeds Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond, but this setup order is distinct from turn order.
First player to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; no need to finish action, phase, or turn.
Choose a clearing with your warriors or Vagabond pawn and an enemy there as defender. Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.

answer.part: Battle effect and removal effect ordering
answer.ruling: For before-roll and after-roll effects at same timing, attacker chooses order if both sides have effects. The side taking hits chooses order of effects triggered by its own pieces' removal.
In Count Hits, add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), then subtract hits ignored by effects.

answer.part: Non-Vagabond item craft token and VP
answer.ruling: Item card requires corresponding item token in map supply. Take it from map supply into crafting faction's Crafted Items box; crafting card is discarded. Usually score VP printed on card, except Eyrie scores one VP instead (with Builder exception). Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items.

answer.part: Eyrie and Alliance crafting pieces, suit, question mark
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy, one piece per icon in a clearing matching that icon's suit; a crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing it occupies. Three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters; with no base keep at most five and discard overflow, with any base there is no cap. Alliance may craft, Mobilize, and Train in any order and number during Daylight; it need not finish all crafting first.

answer.part: Eyrie Evening scoring and draw after Turmoil
answer.ruling: Score VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses, discard to five. The full normal Evening including those steps occurs after Turmoil.

Exhaust one face-up, undamaged sword to initiate Battle. An exhausted undamaged sword may count toward rolled-hit maximum, but it cannot pay the action cost because paying requires a face-up undamaged item.
Each turn proceeds Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Turns pass clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise begins Birdsong.
For each hit, choose one undamaged item and move it to Damaged box without changing its face. An already-damaged item cannot take another hit; if no undamaged items remain, ignore excess hits.

Alliance may take up to its number of officers in Evening military operations, in any order and repetition; an operation does not consume an officer. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
Vagabond takes Daylight actions in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; there is no fixed action order and action types may be repeated.

Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing (or, only if that faction has no warriors there, another piece of that faction). Exhausting requires a face-up, undamaged item, so an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Daylight Strike.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Daylight Strike.
